title: Drug target enzymes, ALOX5 and ACE

segs.text: Section nineteen. Drug target enzymes, five lipoxygenase and A C E. Enzymes can be drug targets too, and both examples break the expected pattern. The A L O X five variant changes response to a drug without changing the disease. The A C E variant does not seem to change how well the drug works, but probably changes the risk of adverse effects.

Five lipoxygenase, the A L O X five gene, has a role in asthma and is the target of five lipoxygenase inhibitors. The variant is tandem repeats in the promoter. The five repeat allele is thought to increase expression, and only subjects with at least one five repeat allele responded to the inhibitor. The repeat changes the amount of the drug's target, so it changes how the inhibitor works, but it has no link to asthma severity. A polymorphism need not cause the disease to affect its treatment.

The A C E variant is not a single nucleotide polymorphism. It is an insertion or deletion, an indel, in intron sixteen, associated with plasma A C E levels, and it is tied to the risk of side effects of A C E inhibitors, not to their efficacy.

Cough occurs in about ten percent of patients on A C E inhibitors; angioedema in only zero point one to zero point two percent. Because angioedema is so rare, a study would need a very large population to enroll enough cases to genotype, so the link is unproven and genotyping cannot yet keep at risk patients off the class. If it were proven, a carrier of the indel could have hypertension treated another way.
